notes.MC: Honest ratio: the counted ring is 12 chairs, 7 seated children, 1 child standing, 4 spare chairs claimed by coats, a handbag and RESERVED slips: four spare chairs for the one child out, matching about 4 homes nobody lives in per homeless household (counting second homes). No number written in either image; the only text is RESERVED. Children are always from behind or seen from directly above (party hats, crowns of heads) to stay clear of refusals. Keeps Jack's night/fluorescent-teal/cheap-film look: the hall at night, one flickering tube, black windows.
notes.ST: Kept Jack's look: the only light is the pool's own underwater lamps, which give the fluorescent teal for free, plus one sodium lamp for contrast; cheap night colour film and grain. Honesty to the numbers: rather than one lone family facing an endless deck (which would overstate it), the reveal shows a few families standing along the deck with roughly four towelled loungers for every family, the about-4-to-1 ratio counting second homes. If the director wants the 2-to-1 (long-term empty only) version, change 'about four' to 'about two' in the reveal. Children appear only as small figures from behind, far off, with bags; no faces, no brands on towels or bags, no numbers in either image.
notes.HW: Kept the red tick on purpose: green is common in UK schools now, but red is the tick everyone recognises in one look and it is the only warm colour against the teal, so the eye lands on it. Switch to green if Jack wants it truer to a current classroom. The one-number rule: the setup shows no digits at all (four drawn houses, one drawn family, the question written in words), so the reveal's '1' is the only number in either image. Question shortened to 'How many families have no home?' so the model can render it. No child is shown, only their things (pencil, rubber, crayons, a juice beaker). Look: night kitchen under a cheap fluorescent tube, teal cast, grain, as the reference; no break from it.
notes.SO: Look kept: night, cold fluorescent teal, cheap colour film grain, the corner-shop register of the reference doorway photo. Honesty to the ratio: the reveal asks for 'enough to refill that shelf about four times over' (the 4-to-1 counting second homes), never 'endless'; if a 2-to-1 version is wanted, change 'about four times over' to 'at least twice over'. No numbers drawn in either image; the only text is the handwritten card 'SORRY, SOLD OUT'. Boxes are plain unbranded brown cases with no labels, to avoid fake brands. The one person is seen from behind only. The stockroom is clearly the same shop (same teal tubes) so the cut reads as one place. The setup frames the doorway at the far end of the aisle so the camera drift to it in animation is natural.
notes.AL: Setup and reveal are the same gate from the same spot so the cut reads as a head-turn: first the person and the letter, then what is behind the fence. Honesty to the ratio: the reveal shows a handful of tended plots (a few small lit sheds) against roughly twice as many gone wild, not a whole field of dereliction, so it reads 'more than enough' without exaggerating. Only text: the letter line 'You are on our waiting list' (no number in either image). The look holds Jack's night teal: one cold fluorescent lamp on a pole, cheap colour film grain, lonely. Slight break: it is an edge-of-town outdoor space rather than a shopfront, so the teal comes from a single security lamp and the sky stays deep blue-black. No faces; the figure is seen from behind.
notes.PB: Honesty to the numbers: the reveal shows exactly FOUR untouched named party bags left on the table for the ONE child leaving with nothing, which is the 4-to-1 ratio counting second homes (571,079 homes that are nobody's main home vs 134,210 homeless households); the narrator's 'already had one' maps the extra bags to second homes and empties. The setup establishes the hall and the crowded table (the plenty); the reveal is the end of the night. No numbers written in either image, so nothing can misread. The child is only ever a small figure from behind in a coat (refusal risk with children), no faces; names on the bags are invented first names, no brands. Look follows Jack's reference: night, cheap colour film, grain, cold fluorescent teal, slightly eerie; the party colours (balloons, bunting) are kept but drained under the tubes, which helps the 'party's over' feeling. The bags carry no handwritten text in the reveal beyond a name each, so the model has little lettering to garble.
